skillSays: Animate between UI states with the browser's native document.startViewTransition; declare what animates with view-transition names/classes and style it in CSS.
Every transition must say what it communicates: shared element, reveal, list identity, enter/exit, or route change; if it says nothing, do not add it.
Use the provided timing vars (exit 150ms, enter 210ms, move 400ms) and ready-made recipes: fade, slide-up/down, scale-in/out, morph.
Give each list item its own unique name so siblings glide into their new spot; wrap displaced content so it glides instead of jumping.
Make the root a live capture (hide old root, no root animation) and set ::view-transition { pointer-events: none } so the page stays interactive and hover keeps working.
Always include the reduced-motion block; unsupported browsers just skip the animation.

changes: Toast and the booked slot change in ONE startViewTransition call: toast has view-transition-name: toast, class slide-up/slide-down; the slot is a named update so it cross-fades.

Enter uses the slide-up recipe: opacity 210ms ease-in plus translateY(32px) 400ms ease-in; exit uses slide-down: 150ms ease-out (fade + 16px). Dropped the recipe's 150ms enter delay because nothing is exiting beside it.
Root is live (::view-transition-old(root) hidden, new(root) animation none) and ::view-transition has pointer-events: none.
Reduced-motion block from the skill zeroes all view-transition durations.
examples.note: Plain JS on the browser View Transitions API, no React: the skill's <ViewTransition> is a thin wrapper over document.startViewTransition, so the demo calls it directly with view-transition-name/-class.

changes: Menu is a named view transition (menu) toggled with hidden inside startViewTransition; it uses the skill's scale recipes: scale-in 210ms ease-out from scale(0.85), scale-out 150ms ease-in.
transform-origin: top right set on both pseudo-elements so it grows from the trigger; enter delay removed (no paired exit).
The hover highlight inside the menu is deliberately not a view transition: unnamed content stays live under the transition.
view-transition-class holds both scale-in and scale-out so one element covers entering and leaving.
List identity pattern: every task li gets a unique view-transition-name (task-1, task-2, ...) so siblings glide up on removal with the 400ms ease-in-out group animation (--duration-move).
New rows use class fade-in (210ms ease-out), removed rows use fade-out (150ms ease-in), set per transition, because a class on an element that exists in both states would flash.
Layout displacement morph: the footer and the count pill are named too, so they glide or cross-fade instead of jumping; the empty-state is a named enter/exit.
Check-off is an update on the named row, so it cross-fades at 210ms; the root stays live so the typed input keeps updating.
